subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should OpenClaw accept failing `openclaw gateway install --force` earlier when `gateway.auth.mode=none` and the effective bind is non-loopback?
rationale: The patch is functionally clean, but it changes an install/refresh API surface by turning an existing runtime refusal into an install-time operator action requirement.

options.title: Accept earlier install block
options.body: Merge the PR as the narrower guard because it matches the existing runtime security refusal and gives a clearer remediation before service rewrite.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run proving the branch behavior in the actual service refresh path before merge.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Keep the PR paused if maintainers want the broader update mutation claim reproduced before accepting this narrower install-boundary fix.

recommendation.title: Accept earlier install block
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as the narrower guard because it matches the existing runtime security refusal and gives a clearer remediation before service rewrite.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across Gateway install, startup, and auth-boundary decisions in the affected files.
